tracks.narration: How big can the dot product of two vectors get?
Fix the lengths of u and v. The lengths of u and v multiplied set a ceiling — the dot product can never exceed it in size.
Spin v around. The dot product rises and falls, but the trace stays bounded between plus and minus the ceiling — it kisses the bound exactly when v lines up with u.
Equality holds when u and v are parallel — same direction gives plus the ceiling, opposite directions give minus. Anything in between misses.
Cauchy and Schwarz: the dot product is squeezed by the lengths. That is what makes cosine of theta a real number between minus one and one.
